title: When Are 1099 Forms Due for Contractors?
summary: Know when 1099 forms are due in 2026. Key deadlines for businesses and contractors filing 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC forms.
body_markdown:
Knowing when 1099 forms are due sounds simple enough until you're juggling different forms, different deadlines, and a calendar where January 31 falls on a Saturday. The 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC don't share the same rules, and a mix-up between them is one of the most common reasons businesses end up paying IRS penalties they didn't see coming. Here's a clear look at this year's actual deadlines.


**TLDR:**


- The 1099-NEC deadline for tax year 2025 is February 2, 2026 (shifted from January 31, which falls on a Saturday).
- Filing 10 or more combined information returns requires electronic submission via the IRS IRIS system; the legacy FIRE system closes December 31, 2026.
- Late 1099s cost $60 per form at minimum under IRC Sections 6721 and 6722, with penalties doubling when both the return and payee copy are missing.
- Electronic filing auto-routes data to 40+ states via the IRS CF/SF program; New York, Pennsylvania, and Oregon require separate direct portal submissions.
- Dots routes payout and 1099 compliance through one API contract, collecting W-9s and filing forms automatically based on payment history.


## What Is a 1099 Form and Who Needs to File One


The 1099 designation covers IRS information returns reporting income paid to[independent contractors](https://usedots.com/solutions/contractors) and vendors. This obligation applies strictly to payments made for a trade or business. Personal payments fall outside these rules.


Businesses, LLCs, and nonprofits must file these forms. You skip reporting payments to most corporations, with statutory exceptions for attorney fees and medical payments.


Your 1099 filing obligation triggers once you pay a non-corporate vendor or independent contractor $600 or more in a calendar year. Below that threshold, no form is required. Track cumulative payments across the year: a single $400 payment in March and a $300 payment in August to the same contractor cross the $600 mark and require a filing.


## 1099-NEC vs. 1099-MISC: Key Differences


The[1099 form for contractors](https://usedots.com/blog/which-1099-form-for-contractors/) reports nonemployee compensation paid to independent contractors. Form 1099-MISC logs distinct payouts like rent, royalties, and awards. Third-party network payments require Form 1099-K.


When are 1099 forms due? These documents carry different IRS filing schedules. Payers often make the costly mistake of applying the 1099-MISC extended electronic deadline to the 1099-NEC. The 1099-NEC carries a single January 31 cutoff for both paper and electronic submissions: no extension applies. The 1099-MISC, by contrast, gives filers until March 31 for electronic IRS submissions, though recipient copies are still due January 31. Confusing the two means filing the wrong form or missing the tighter NEC deadline, both of which trigger penalties under IRC Sections 6721 and 6722.


## 1099 Filing Deadlines for Tax Year 2025 (Filed in 2026)


You must track specific calendar adjustments to stay compliant. Because January 31 and February 28 fall on Saturdays in 2026, the agency[moved these cutoffs](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1099gi) to the next business day.


The 1099-NEC due date 2026 for recipient copies and IRS submissions is February 2, 2026, because January 31 falls on a Saturday and the agency moves the cutoff to the next business day. This single deadline covers both paper and electronic filings; unlike Form 1099-MISC, the 1099-NEC carries no extended electronic submission date. Form 1099-MISC recipient copies follow the same February 2 adjustment, while paper IRS submissions are due March 2 and electronic IRS submissions are due March 31.

## 1099 Filing Deadlines for Tax Year 2026 (Filed in 2027)


For 2026 payments, the standard January 31 deadline falls on a Sunday. This moves your compliance dates:


- Form 1099-NEC recipient copies and IRS filings are due February 1, 2027.
- Form 1099-MISC recipient copies are due February 1, 2027.
- Form 1099-MISC paper IRS filings are due March 1, 2027; electronic IRS filings are due March 31, 2027.


## W-2 and 1099 Deadlines: What Businesses Need to Know


Businesses paying mixed workforces face a unified cutoff. Understanding[payroll for 1099 employees](https://usedots.com/blog/how-to-do-payroll-1099-employees/) helps clarify how the deadline for W-2 to be sent out 2026 matches your 1099-NEC obligations. You must submit Form W-2 (Wage and Tax Statement) to employees and the Social Security Administration (SSA) by January 31 for paper and electronic submissions.


While these dates align, reporting pathways separate your filings: W-2s route to the Social Security Administration (SSA), while 1099-NEC forms go directly to the IRS. You submit W-2s through the SSA's Business Services Online portal, whereas 1099-NEC filings use the IRS IRIS system. Keeping these submission channels distinct prevents misdirected filings, which the IRS treats as non-filed returns and penalizes accordingly under IRC Sections 6721 and 6722.


## IRS Electronic Filing Requirements and the FIRE-to-IRIS Transition


Businesses submitting 10 or more information returns annually must learn how to file 1099 electronically with the IRS, and[APIs for automating 1099 tax filing](https://usedots.com/blog/best-apis-automating-1099-tax-filing-contractor-payments/) can simplify this process. This threshold aggregates all tax forms. Processing five 1099-NEC documents and five 1099-MISC documents hits the 10-return limit.


The legacy FIRE system closes December 31, 2026. After that date, all electronic 1099 submissions must route through the IRS IRIS (Information Returns Intake System) portal. IRIS accepts filings at no cost and supports the full range of 1099 form types. Businesses that have not yet registered for IRIS should do so before the FIRE shutdown to avoid a gap in their electronic filing capability.


## State 1099 Filing Requirements


The IRS Combined Federal/State Filing (CF/SF) program forwards your 1099-NEC form data to over 40 participating states automatically. This routing only activates when you file electronically. Paper submissions bypass this system, forcing manual mailings to each jurisdiction.


Not every state participates. New York, Pennsylvania, and Oregon mandate direct portal submissions outside the federal network. For payees earning across multiple jurisdictions, see the[1099-NEC multi-state guide for creators](https://usedots.com/blog/creator-1099-nec-multi-state-guide/) . These independent state filing obligations carry their own deadlines and penalties, separate from and in addition to any IRS assessment. Confirm each state's requirements before your federal filing date, since some state portals close earlier than the federal cutoff.


## Penalties for Late or Missing 1099 Forms


Your[1099 filing penalties](https://usedots.com/blog/what-to-know-about-1099-filing-penalties/) quickly multiply. The IRS penalizes payers twice under IRC Sections 6721 and 6722 for failing to file the return and failing to furnish the payee statement.


Late fees escalate based on timing, as outlined in the[IRS 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC instructions](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1099mec) :


- $60 per form when filed within 30 days of the deadline, rising to $130 per form after 30 days, and $330 per form for returns never filed or filed after August 1. Because IRC Sections 6721 and 6722 each impose their own assessment (one for failing to file with the IRS and one for failing to furnish the payee statement), a single missed 1099-NEC can generate $660 in penalties for that one form. A business with 50 unfiled forms could face over $33,000 in combined assessments before any willful-neglect multipliers apply.


## How to Request a Filing Extension


You can request a 30-day extension for the 1099 filing deadline 2026 by submitting Form 8809 before your due date. For teams managing scale,[automated compliance and tax management](https://usedots.com/blog/automated-compliance-tax-management-contractor-payments/) for contractor payments reduces deadline risk. Extensions are never automatic for the 1099-NEC form 2026, which demands documented hardship circumstances.


Form 8809 only delays IRS submission. You still must deliver recipient copies to payees by the original January 31 deadline: extensions do not apply to payee statements. If you miss the recipient copy deadline, IRC Sections 6721 and 6722 penalties still accrue on the unfiled payee statement even while your IRS submission remains in extension. File Form 8809 early; waiting until the due date leaves no buffer if the IRS rejects your request.


## Common 1099 Filing Mistakes to Avoid


Filing exact returns is mandatory. Errors trigger expensive notices.


- Missing the 1099-NEC due date 2026 (January 31) happens when confusing it with the 1099-MISC. Businesses focused on[tax compliance for 1099 workers](https://usedots.com/blog/remaining-tax-compliant-when-employing-1099-workers/) should note the 1099-NEC form carries no extended electronic submission date.
- Submitting mismatched TINs generates IRS CP2100 B-notices, which require you to notify the affected payee and begin 24% backup withholding on future payments if the mismatch isn't resolved. Run TIN matching through the IRS e-services portal before your first payout to a new contractor: catching a name-number mismatch at onboarding costs nothing, while correcting it after a B-notice triggers mandatory withholding that disrupts your payment workflow and the payee's cash flow.

Getting your 1099 filings right is about knowing which form applies, when it's due, and how your state wants it delivered. Small missteps, like confusing the 1099-NEC deadline with the 1099-MISC window, can lead to penalties that compound quickly. ## FAQ


### When are 1099-NEC forms due for tax year 2025 (filed in 2026)?


The 1099-NEC filing deadline for tax year 2025 falls on February 2, 2026, for both recipient copies and IRS submissions, because January 31 lands on a Saturday in 2026. This single deadline applies regardless of whether you file on paper or electronically. Unlike Form 1099-MISC, the 1099-NEC form carries no extended electronic submission date.


### Can I file 1099-NEC forms electronically with the IRS for free?


Yes. The IRS IRIS (Information Returns Intake System) portal lets you file 1099-NEC electronically with the IRS at no cost, and it replaces the legacy FIRE system, which closes December 31, 2026. Any business submitting 10 or more information returns annually must file electronically. That threshold counts all form types combined, so five 1099-NEC forms plus five 1099-MISC forms triggers the electronic filing requirement.


### What happens if I miss the 1099-NEC filing deadline in 2026?


The IRS issues two separate penalties under IRC Sections 6721 and 6722: one for failing to file the return with the IRS and one for failing to furnish the payee statement. A single missed form can generate two penalty assessments. Fees escalate based on how late you file, starting at $60 per form, which means a batch of unfiled 1099-NEC forms compounds quickly into a material compliance cost.


### 1099-NEC multi-state filing: do I need to file separately with each state?


The IRS Combined Federal/State Filing (CF/SF) program automatically forwards your 1099-NEC data to over 40 participating states, but only when you file electronically. Paper submissions bypass this forwarding entirely and require you to mail separate copies to each state. States like New York, Pennsylvania, and Oregon do not participate in CF/SF, so they require direct portal submissions outside the federal network regardless of how you file.

Catching TIN mismatches before payout batches clear also blocks IRS CP2100 notices, which trigger mandatory 24% backup withholding on future payments to a flagged worker.
